items.fromString:
When configuring an instance of the NetworkObserver with a mirror or otherwise custom images it is not intuitive, especially with image shas.


Example with hack to include a sha256 image reference.


{code:yaml}---
apiVersion: observability.skupper.io/v2alpha1
kind: NetworkObserver
metadata:
  name: customimages
spec:
  image:
    repository: "mirror.acme.org/rhsi-network-observer@sha256"
    tag: "20c3f199f0647914d0495bcb282a5f3e9f926c5cc8a42f89a02d1546730ba9ed"

{code}



Suggestion is an all-in-one image name {{“mirror.acme.org/rhsi-network-observer@sha256:aaaaa..."}}, or at least a dedicated space for a shasum.
items.toString:
When configuring an instance of the NetworkObserver with a mirror or otherwise custom images it is not intuitive, especially with image shas. Also applies to other images configurable in the NetworkObserver - prometheus, oauth proxy.


Example with hack to include a sha256 image reference.


{code:yaml}---
apiVersion: observability.skupper.io/v2alpha1
kind: NetworkObserver
metadata:
  name: customimages
spec:
  image:
    repository: "mirror.acme.org/rhsi-network-observer@sha256"
    tag: "20c3f199f0647914d0495bcb282a5f3e9f926c5cc8a42f89a02d1546730ba9ed"

{code}



Suggestion is an all-in-one image name {{“mirror.acme.org/rhsi-network-observer@sha256:aaaaa..."}}, or at least a dedicated space for a shasum.

h2. Problem Description

Pre-existing invalid upgrade paths, referred to as "stranded bundles," were exposed in the operator catalog content. This exposure occurred due to the OCP 4.21 OPM tooling alignment, specifically the upgrade to OPM v1.58.0+, which now includes new quality gates to validate and block these invalid paths.

h2. Steps to Reproduce

[Please Provide]

h2. Expected Behavior

h1. Users should be able to upgrade off the affected versions of the operators and not be "stranded"
h1. The operator catalog should pass the new quality gates instituted by the OPM v1.58.0+ tooling
h1. The OCP 4.22 catalog should successfully bootstrap

h2. Actual Behavior

_Catalog Test Failures:_
An upgrade to the latest OPM tooling (v1.58.0+) for OCP 4.21 is causing widespread failures in the catalog tests. This is because the new OPM version is correctly identifying the pre-existing invalid upgrade paths.

_Catalog Blockage:_
The new quality gates implemented in OPM v1.58.0+ are blocking the entire catalog due to the presence of these "stranded bundles."

h2. Error Messages / Logs

_Type of Failure:_
The new OPM tooling is causing "widespread failures in our catalog tests"

_Stranded bundles assessment spreadsheet:_
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ngHlFDOflLkpzf7Fd3_AAet_wqx65vjV8PkpHPonO2w/

h2. Root Cause

_Root Cause Identified:_
The failure is due to the tooling "correctly identifying these 'stranded bundles'"

_Description of "Stranded Bundles":_
These are defined as pre-existing "invalid upgrade paths" in the catalog content.

h2. Impact

* Blocking OCP 4.22 catalog bootstrap
* Widespread catalog test failures
* Multiple operators affected with invalid upgrade paths

## Users should be able to upgrade off the affected versions of the operators and not be "stranded"
2. The operator catalog should pass the new quality gates instituted by the OPM v1.58.0+ tooling

h2. Actual Behavior

An upgrade to the latest OPM tooling (v1.58.0+) for OCP 4.21 is causing widespread failures in the catalog tests. This is because the new OPM version is correctly identifying the pre-existing invalid upgrade paths.

*Catalog Blockage:*
The new quality gates implemented in OPM v1.58.0+ are blocking the entire catalog due to the presence of these "stranded bundles."

*Root Cause Identified:*
The failure is due to the tooling "correctly identifying these 'stranded bundles'"

These are defined as pre-existing "invalid upgrade paths" in the catalog content.

h2. Impact
* Blocking OCP 4.22 catalog bootstrap
* Widespread catalog test failures
* Multiple operators affected with invalid upgrade paths

# Replace <your-namespace> with the site namespace.
kubectl rollout restart deployment skupper-network-observer -n <your-namespace>

items.fromString:
When deploying Skupper using the *cluster-scoped* YAML installation method on Azure Kubernetes Service, the skupper-controller seems failing to process Skupper custom resources.

The controller pod logs show the following message, indicating it is ignoring resources it should be managing:
{quote}msg="Ignoring resources in namespace controlled by another controller" component=kube.controller namespace=van-tst controlled-by=van-tst/skupper-controller
{quote}
It is possible to fix this issue by adding the WATCH_NAMESPACE env variable with empty value (two single quotes) to the controller deployment:
{quote}env:

- name: WATCH_NAMESPACE
   value: ''
{quote}
Is this the correct approach. Could this be added to cluster-scoped YAML installation guide?

items.fromString:
If you create a listener resource before creating a site in a namespace, the listener might not work as expected and you might see excessive logging like:

```
2025-09-25 00:41:43.870905 +0000 FLOW_LOG (info) LOG [89855:273642] BEGIN END parent=89855:0 logSeverity=3 logText=LOG_TCP_ADAPTOR: Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082) sourceFile=/remote-source/skupper-router/app/src/adaptors/adaptor_listener.c sourceLine=172

2025-09-25 00:52:15.490647 +0000 TCP_ADAPTOR (error) Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082)

```

To workaround this issue, delete and recreate any listener resources.

To avoid this issue, always create a site before creating other resources.
items.toString:
If you create a listener resource before creating a site in a namespace, the listener might not work as expected and you might see excessive router logging like:

```
2025-09-25 00:41:43.870905 +0000 FLOW_LOG (info) LOG [89855:273642] BEGIN END parent=89855:0 logSeverity=3 logText=LOG_TCP_ADAPTOR: Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082) sourceFile=/remote-source/skupper-router/app/src/adaptors/adaptor_listener.c sourceLine=172

2025-09-25 00:52:15.490647 +0000 TCP_ADAPTOR (error) Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082)

```

To workaround this issue, delete and recreate any listener resources.

To avoid this issue, always create a site and wait for the site status `ready` before creating other resources.

If you create a listener resource before creating a site in a namespace, the listener might not work as expected and you might see excessive logging like:

```
2025-09-25 00:41:43.870905 +0000 FLOW_LOG (info) LOG [89855:273642] BEGIN END parent=89855:0 logSeverity=3 logText=LOG_TCP_ADAPTOR: Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082) sourceFile=/remote-source/skupper-router/app/src/adaptors/adaptor_listener.c sourceLine=172

2025-09-25 00:52:15.490647 +0000 TCP_ADAPTOR (error) Listener backend: proactor listener error on backend:8082: proton:io (Cannot assign requested address - listen on backend:8082)

```

To workaround this issue, delete and recreate any listener resources.

To avoid this issue, always create a site before creating other resources.
